reading: Three colour bands per row (left colour at the left border, a middle colour, a right colour). In each row the middle-colour run is slid horizontally so its right end sits on the rightmost column shared by every row's middle run (clamped at column 0 if the run is too long); the left colour fills the rest of that row's left+middle span.

slots.subject: the middle-colour run in each row
slots.anchor: min over rows of the run's right end (a column every run contains)
slots.action: shift run so right end = anchor, start clamped at 0
slots.filler: left-border colour fills vacated cells of the left+middle span

slots.subject: the middle-colour run in each row
slots.anchor: min over rows of the run's right end (a column every run contains)
slots.action: shift run so right end = anchor, start clamped at 0
slots.filler: left-border colour fills vacated cells of the left+middle span

why: every row keeps its run lengths and its right-colour cells; middle runs end at the shared column
invariants: count of left-colour cells per row

reading: Two rectangles; one carries a one-cell-wide tail of its own colour reaching to the other. That rectangle slides along its tail until it touches the other rectangle, and the tail is erased.

slots.subject: rectangle body of the object that has a 1-wide tail (cells with bg on both perpendicular sides)
rectangle body of the object that has a 1-wide tail (cells with bg on both perpendicular sides)

why: moved body keeps its shape and ends adjacent to the other rectangle; distance moved = tail length

reading: The input is three 4x4 panels of 5 separated by 0 columns, each with a hole pattern. Each panel maps to a colour by its hole pattern and the 3x3 output has row i filled with panel i's colour.

slots.panels: three 4x4 panels cut by full 0 separator columns
slots.key: no hole -> 2; 2x2 centre hole -> 8; 2x2 hole at bottom centre -> 4; holes in middle of left and right edges -> 3
slots.output: 3x3 grid, row i = colour of panel i

reading: Each isolated coloured cell draws a line of its colour right to the grid border, then turns down along the last column, stopping just above the row of the next marker below (or at the bottom).

slots.leg1: rightward from marker to right border
slots.leg2: down the last column from the marker row
slots.stop: row before the next marker's row, else bottom border

why: every marker row is filled from the marker to the right border; last column below each marker takes that marker's colour until the next marker row
invariants: cells left of each marker unchanged

frame.verb: fit shape into frame, colour by nearest side

reading: Count each colour's cells. Output has one column per colour sorted by count descending; each column holds its colour count times from the top, rest 0; height = largest count.

slots.size: rows = max count, cols = number of colours

reading: The grid is split into two background regions (8 and 1), each holding 2-coloured blocks. In the 8 region every block slides left to the region's left edge; in the 1 region every block slides right to the region's right edge.
verb: push to side by region colour
why: each 2 block keeps its shape and ends touching the panel edge: left edge when panel bg is 8, right edge when panel bg is 1
invariants: number of 2 cells per row within each panel

reading: Two big background regions each hold an inner rectangle of another colour with one-cell defects (notches or bumps) on its edge. Each defect becomes a 2-cell stub perpendicular to the edge (defect cell plus the next cell across the edge) in the other big region's colour.

slots.regions: the two large coloured regions (e.g. 8 and 4)
slots.defects: single-cell notch into or bump out of a rectangle edge
slots.mark: defect cell + adjacent cell across the edge (outward for notch, inward for bump)
slots.colour: the colour of the other big region

reading: Every 3 cell slides left along its row until it hits an 8 or the left border; each row moves independently.
why: each row's run of 3 keeps its length and ends adjacent to the first 8 to its left (or at column 0)

reading: Noisy 0/5 grid with scattered 2 cells. Around certain 5 cells, the 3x3 window contains no 0 and holds 2s; in each such window (the one with most 2s among overlapping ones) the centre becomes 4 and every non-2 cell becomes 7.

slots.windows: 3x3 windows centred on a 5, containing no 0 and at least one 2; keep the window with most 2s among overlapping candidates
slots.ring: non-2 cells of the window recoloured 7
